    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
    [IsPartialCube G] (h_helly : OppositeSemicubeHellyProperty G) :
    IsAntipodal G ↔ PairwiseIsomorphicOppositeSemicubes G
directions.proof_strategy: Formalize partial cubes as isometric subgraphs of hypercubes, define the Djoković-Winkler relation Θ and Θ-classes, formalize semicubes W_ab and W_ba, define antipodal graphs and the opposite-semicube Helly property. Prove the forward direction by showing antipodality implies isomorphic opposite semicubes. For the reverse direction, assume the Helly property and isomorphic opposite semicubes, then construct an antipodal mapping using the non-empty intersections guaranteed by the Helly property to show every vertex has a unique antipode.
directions.title: Antipodality Characterization via Opposite-Semicube Helly Property

directions.description: For a geometric family of principally polarized abelian varieties over Q, the average size of the ℓ-Selmer group is unbounded if and only if the product of local Tamagawa ratios exceeds 1. Specifically, for the family of quadratic twists {E_d : d squarefree} of an elliptic curve E/Q at a prime ℓ of good reduction, the average |Sel_ℓ(E_d)| over |d| ≤ X is unbounded as X → ∞ if and only if ∏_p c_p(E, ℓ) > 1, where c_p(E, ℓ) is the local factor from the Greenberg–Wiles formula. The paper proves this for families with constant ℓ-torsion Galois module; the conjecture asserts it holds unconditionally.

directions.description: For every elliptic curve E/Q with analytic rank 0 and every non-trivial finite abelian group G, there exist infinitely many G-extensions F/Q such that E(F) is finite (equivalently, rank E(F) = 0). This removes the 'no exceptional primes' condition from the paper's Corollary 1.3 and the 'sufficiently large prime factors' condition from Theorem 1.1, yielding the full generalization of the David-Fearnley-Kisilevsky conjecture from quadratic to all finite abelian extensions.

directions.description: A tournament T is cycle Mengerian (CM) if for every nonnegative integral weight function w on arcs, the maximum cycle packing size ν_w(T) equals its fractional relaxation ν*_w(T). T is cycle ideal (CI) if the minimum feedback arc set weight τ_w(T) equals its fractional relaxation τ*_w(T) for all such w. Since ν*_w = τ*_w by LP duality, CM and CI together yield the min-max relation τ_w = ν_w. The conjecture is that these two integrality properties coincide: a tournament is CM if and only if it is CI.

Use the structural characterization of CM tournaments by Chen et al. (2020) to verify that every CM tournament satisfies the CI property (τ*_w = τ_w) by exhibiting integral optimal solutions to the FAS LP, and conversely that every CI tournament satisfies the CM property by showing the cycle packing LP has integral optima. The key bridge is the LP duality equality ν*_w = τ*_w and the chain of inequalities ν_w ≤ ν*_w = τ*_w ≤ τ_w.
directions.title: Cycle Mengerian and Cycle Ideal Equivalence for Tournaments

The conjecture asserts that this condition is also necessary: if a countable FAC poset P does contain such a saturated chain, then P fails to satisfy the Aharoni-Korman conjecture. The construction likely involves adapting the known counterexamples to the original Aharoni-Korman conjecture, using the specific structure of ⊕_{x∈ω} D_x to control all possible chain-antichain interactions.

directions.description: For any convex polytope P in ℝ^� (with e = d+1 being the embedding dimension), the set of centerpoints of P coincides with the floating body of P at level 1/(d+1). Specifically, a point x is a centerpoint of P (meaning every closed halfspace containing x contains at least a 1/(d+1) fraction of the volume of P) if and only if x belongs to the floating body F_{1/(d+1)}(P), defined as the intersection of all closed halfspaces H⁺ such that vol(P \ H⁺) ≤ (1/(d+1)) · vol(P). The paper establishes this equivalence and further shows that for polytopes this set is semialgebraic.
domain_bridges: Convex geometry ↔ Combinatorial topology ↔ Semialgebraic geometry ↔ Measure theory on polytopes
directions.lean_theorem_stub:
theorem centerpoint_eq_floating_body {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) (P : Polytope (Fin d → ℝ)) (hP : Convex P ∧ IsPolytope P) : centerpointSet P = floatingBody P (1 / (d + 1)) := by
 sorry
directions.proof_strategy: The proof proceeds by double inclusion. (⊆): If x is a centerpoint, then every halfspace H⁺ containing x satisfies vol(P ∩ H⁺) ≥ vol(P)/(d+1), equivalently vol(P \ H⁺) ≤ vol(P)·d/(d+1); but the floating body condition requires vol(P \ H⁺) ≤ vol(P)/(d+1) for the halfspaces defining it, so one must show that a centerpoint lies in every halfspace whose complementary cap has volume ≤ vol(P)/(d+1). (⊇): Conversely, if x ∈ F_{1/(d+1)}(P), then x lies in every halfspace H⁺ with vol(P \ H⁺) ≤ vol(P)/(d+1), and one must show this forces every halfspace through x to capture at least 1/(d+1) of the volume. The key technical ingredient is that the cap-volume function is piecewise rational on the arrangement of oriented hyperplanes determined by the polytope's facets, which makes both sets explicitly semialgebraic and allows their coincidence to be verified.
directions.title: Centerpoint-Floating Body Equivalence for Convex Polytopes

directions.description: For a squarefree integer N > 1 with an even number of prime factors, and a positive divisor d | N, let w_d denote the corresponding Atkin-Lehner involution on the Shimura curve X_N. The genus of the quotient X_N / ⟨w_d⟩ is determined by the Riemann-Hurwitz formula applied to the double cover X_N → X_N / ⟨w_d⟩, where the number of fixed points of w_d equals the number of optimal embeddings of a certain quadratic order into the quaternion order, expressible via class numbers. The conjecture is: X_N / ⟨w_d⟩ has genus zero if and only if (N, d) belongs to an explicit finite list, which strictly contains the list {(6,6), (10,10), (22,22)} arising from genus-zero X_N alone. This classification is the key structural result enabling the extension of the Giampietro-Darmon factorization beyond the original conjecture.

directions.proof_strategy: First formalize the genus formula for Shimura curves X_N of discriminant N (already explicit in the literature, e.g., Ogg). Then formalize the fixed-point count of Atkin-Lehner involutions w_d in terms of class numbers of imaginary quadratic orders via optimal embedding counts. Apply Riemann-Hurwitz to the double cover X_N → X_N/⟨w_d⟩ to obtain the genus of the quotient. Finally, enumerate all pairs (N, d) with N squarefree, ω(N) even, d | N, for which the resulting genus is zero, yielding the explicit finite classification.
directions.title: Genus-Zero Classification of Atkin-Lehner Quotients of Shimura Curves

directions.description: A Δ-matroid (E, F) is strong (i.e., satisfies the symmetric exchange axiom: for all A, B ∈ F and e ∈ A\B, there exists f ∈ B\A such that A △ {e,f} ∈ F and B △ {e,f} ∈ F) if and only if it contains no peerless antipode. Here, an antipode of a feasible set A with respect to an element e is a feasible set B obtained from A by exchanging e for some f, and a peerless antipode is one that is unique in a specific local sense within the feasible set system. This equivalence provides a local obstruction characterization for the global symmetric exchange property, analogous to how local submodularity characterizes global submodularity for rank functions.
domain_bridges: Tropical geometry (peerless antipode equations as tropicalization of orthogonal Grassmannian quadratics)
directions.lean_theorem_stub:
theorem strong_delta_matroid_iff_no_peerless_antipodes
    {E : Type*} [Fintype E] [DecidableEq E]
    (D : DeltaMatroid E) :
    D.IsStrong ↔ ¬HasPeerlessAntipode D := by
  sorry
directions.proof_strategy: Forward direction (strong ⟹ no peerless antipode): Assume symmetric exchange holds and suppose for contradiction that a peerless antipode exists at some feasible set A with element e. Use the symmetric exchange property between A and any other feasible set witnessing the peerless configuration to construct a second antipode, contradicting peerlessness. Backward direction (no peerless antipode ⟹ strong): Assume no peerless antipode exists and suppose symmetric exchange fails for some A, B ∈ F with e ∈ A\B. Show that the failure produces a peerless antipode: the element e at A has at most one viable exchange partner f ∈ B\A with A △ {e,f} ∈ F, and the absence of any other witness forces this antipode to be peerless, contradicting the hypothesis.
directions.title: Strong Δ-matroids are characterized by the absence of peerless antipodes

directions.description: For every c > 0, there exists K such that any n-vertex graph G with average degree d ≥ K and no cycle of length at least d can be transformed by deleting at most c·d·n edges into a graph whose every connected component has a vertex cover of size at most (1+c)·d.
domain_bridges: Combinatorics → Structural Graph Theory → Approximation/Stability Theory

      (2 * G.edgeFinset.card : ℝ) / (Fintype.card V : ℝ) = (d : ℝ) →
      (∀ l ≥ d, ∀ C : List V, ¬G.IsCycle C l) →
      ∃ H ≤ G,
        (G.edgeFinset.card - H.edgeFinset.card : ℕ) ≤ ⌈c * d * (Fintype.card V : ℝ)⌉₊ ∧
        ∀ C (hC : H.ConnectedComponent C),
          ∃ vc : Finset V,
            vc.card ≤ ⌈(1 + c) * d⌉₊ ∧
            ∀ e ∈ H.edgeSet, (e.1 ∈ vc ∨ e.2 ∈ vc)

Then develop infrastructure for vertex covers of graph components and edge-editing distance. The key structural ingredient is Pokrovskiy's decomposition theorem for bounded-degree trees, which must also be formalized. The proof then proceeds by showing that graphs violating the conclusion have a specific block structure that forces a long cycle.
directions.title: Hyperstability of the Erdős-Gallai Theorem

directions.description: Every symmetric edge polytope of dimension at most 35 has a gamma-positive Ehrhart h*-polynomial; equivalently, 36 is the minimum dimension in which a symmetric edge polytope can fail to be gamma-positive. This is motivated by the paper's construction of a 36-dimensional counterexample to the Ohsugi-Tsuchiya conjecture and by extensive computational evidence for small graphs.

directions.description: For any full-dimensional convex polytope P in R^d, the set of centerpoints of P (points x such that every closed halfspace containing x intersects P in volume at least vol(P)/(d+1)) coincides with the floating body of P at level 1/(d+1). This equivalence bridges the discrete combinatorial notion of centerpoints with the continuous convex-geometric notion of floating bodies, providing a semialgebraic characterization of the centerpoint set.

By the piecewise rational structure of the cap-volume function on the arrangement of oriented hyperplanes, one can find a supporting halfspace through x cutting off less than 1/(d+1) of the volume, contradicting membership in the floating body.

This provides the missing necessary and sufficient condition explicitly noted as unknown in the paper.
